signals.thesis: Lam Research surged +12.7% to a new 52-week high ($364.80) on massive volume (14.5M vs 3.0M avg) as the entire semiconductor equipment complex ripped higher. KLAC led with +12.9%. AMAT +11.2%. The sector is pricing in sustained AI capex demand and a potential CHIPS Act spending acceleration. LRCX's etch and deposition tools are critical for advanced node manufacturing. RSI 67.7 provides room to run before overextension. EMA20 ($316) well below price = momentum confirmed. Entry on pullback to $350 zone gives a clean 2:1 R/R with stop below the breakout level.

GE Aerospace surged +4.4% to $332.76 within striking distance of its 52-week high ($348.48). The aerospace and defense sector benefits from both commercial aviation recovery and defense spending tailwinds. Volume was 3.2M, in line with its average — this is steady institutional buying, not a spike-and-fade. RSI 61.9 is healthy. EMA20 ($315.77) serves as the first pullback target. The entry at $328 on a pullback from today's high gives a clean breakout setup with the stop below the EMA20.

Caterpillar closed at $897.63 (+4.8%) near its 52-week high ($946.83). The construction and mining equipment giant benefits from the US infrastructure spending cycle and global re-industrialization theme. RSI 52.4 is ideal — strong momentum without overextension. ATR 39.2 implies natural price swings, so the $30 stop width (3.4%) is appropriate at 0.77x ATR. The industrial sector led broader market gains (+5% XLI) as the risk appetite snapback from yesterday's RISK-OFF selloff drove rotation into cyclicals.

Merck at $120.76 is approaching its 52-week high ($125.14) after a +1.4% session. RSI 58.8 provides ample headroom. The pharma giant's Keytruda franchise and diversified pipeline make it a defensive growth play — ideal for EARLY RISK-OFF environments. EMA20 ($117.70) provides the pullback floor. Volume at 13.1M was above average, suggesting institutional accumulation. Low correlation with cyclicals (0.13 with LRCX, 0.23 with CAT) adds diversification value to the portfolio.
